newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, downward trend seen to slow.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, downward trend seen to slow.

text.p: Croatian stocks closed mixed on Thursday, with some new losses in hotelier issues, and analysts said the downward trend is likely to continue into the next week, but at a slower pace.
"I expect most firms, particularly hoteliers, to continue losing next week, but not so sharply," said Zoran Ilic from Consult Invest brokerage.
Friday, All Saints' Day, is a public and market holiday in Croatia.
After not being traded for a week, two top losers -- Istrian hoteliers Arenaturist and Laguna -- fell 85 kuna to 155, and 210 kuna to 1,220, respectively. Both were traded on very small volume.
"Our blue chips also lost breath," Ilic said.
Two fully listed Croatian issues -- drug firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka -- closed flat on Thursday.

Zagrebacka, with 18,209 units sold accounted for almost all of the day's trading for the second day running. Total volume of 19,515 shares was down from 25,556 on Wednesday, and turnover was also lower at 18.5 million kuna from 24.1.
Of 10 active issues four were flat, three down and three up.
Ilic said the unusually high trading with Zagrebacka is masking an otherwise very passive market, where most of the transfers were made in symbolic figures.

The market came almost to a total halt after National Security Council last week called for annulment of some 20,000 contracts for purchase of shares at reduced prices under employments buyout scheme.
The contracts were judged illegal for having exceeded the 20,000-German-mark ceiling per person.
"Most investors, particularly foreign, have stopped all orders until the situation with dubious shares is cleared," Ilic said, echoing the comments of other traders.
Varazdinska Banka lead the gainers. The bank's second issue preference stock, which is in short supply, jumped to 714 kuna from 442 in August, on volume of 40 shares.

Kras confectioner recovered 50 kuna to close at 540, but a meagre volume of 20 units leaves open doubts whether it is the end of the fall of one of the most popular Croatian shares from above 700 kuna two weeks ago.
